processing: Little is documented for this cultivar alone. As with other Japanese black teas, leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried in modest batches.
harvest_season: Not well recorded for this cultivar. Japanese black teas are commonly picked in spring and summer.
appearance_dry: Typical of Japanese black tea, dark twisted leaf with a slight sheen.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Japanese black tea, a clear red-amber.
appearance_wet: Typical of Japanese black tea, soft reddish-brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for this cultivar on its own; Japanese black teas are generally mild and rounded rather than harsh.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Japanese black tea. Shorten the steep if the cup turns sharp.

vintage_note: As is usual for Japanese black tea, it would be sold in small lots by harvest year, often with the grower and cultivar named. Drink it within a year or two of picking.
description:
Benihikari is a Japanese cultivar listed for black tea. Its name contains beni, the word for crimson. Details about it are thin.

As with other Japanese black teas, the leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, typically by small makers who name the cultivar as a selling point.

This class usually gives a mild, rounded cup, so you do not need boiling water or a long steep. Start gently and adjust. Ask the grower how it was picked and when, because that will tell you more than the cultivar name.
history: Little is documented about where and when Benihikari was bred, who released it, or how widely it is grown.
